legend: A large verrucous carcinoma of the true cords from a laryngectomy specimen showing a granular, tan, exophytic mass.

Verrucous carcinoma of the larynx. Invasion takes the form of expanded epithelium, which pushes into the stroma in rounded nests that have abundant glassy cytoplasm, round nuclei with prominent nucleoli, and little mitotic activity. There is no stromal reaction.

Verrucous carcinoma with stromally invasive conventional squamous cell carcinoma (or hybrid verrucous carcinoma). The tumour shows a large, maturing verrucous component (above) and small, infiltrative, invasive nests (below).

Thickened, undulating projections and invaginations of well-differentiated squamous epithelium with marked surface keratinization. The invasive area has well-defined pushing borders extending below the level of the surrounding epithelium.
Invaginations and pushing projections of well-differentiated squamous epithelium with one layer of basal cells. The surrounding stroma is densely infiltrated by lymphocytes.

The tumour is composed of a broad mass on the true vocal cord, which extends below the level of the surrounding normal epithelium and which has only mild cytological atypia in the basal aspects, with no stromal reaction.

There is a remarkably thickened squamous epithelium showing hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and parakeratotic crypting. There is church spire–type hyperkeratosis. The adjacent epithelium is not present in this sample, and there is no stroma to show pushing invasion, but the sheer volume of the tumour in this sample is sufficient to move the lesion beyond verrucous hyperplasia.
